notes: A tyrant is as bad as death; nay worse. Death does not approach the truly devout; but the tyrant obeys no laws and kills in murderous fury.

english_title: Let the Ruler Observe Holy Law;
english_translation:
The Holy Law daily in strictness observe
If he who rules the state fails to seek the Divine Way
Day by day that land decays in folly envelopt,
Day by day that ruler's wealth declines and dwindles away.
notes: Let the ruler observe the laws of divine dharma. If he fails, the land falls a prey to destruction.

english_title: Ruler's Duty Towards Men of False Garb
english_translation:
What avails the holy garb if the holy life you refuse?
Theirs the truest garb when outer guise and mind accord;
If the king justly rules and restrains these who go off the holy way
Then he and they attain salvation.
notes: It is the duty of the ruler to spot out the men of false garb, and make them walk the path of purity.

english_translation:
If Brahmins, from folly unredeemed, flaunt the tuft and thread,
That land droops and fades, its ruler's glory runs to waste;
So, scanning deep in Wisdom's light, the King shall clip
The thread and tuft for empty show kept and possessed.
notes: If brahmins flaunting the thread and tuft lead an unholy life, the ruler has a duty to put them back on the straight path. So too with those pretenders who don the holy garb and practise evil ways.

english_title: Ruler's Duty to Impart Wisdom to Erring Brahmins
english_translation:
The senseless fools donning sacred thread and matted locks,
And with chanting phrases pretend to wisdom unpossessed,
Them, the ruler of state shall, with wise men's help, take and test,
And, for the country's good, impart words in wisdom drest.

english_title: Ruler's Duty to Protect Cows, Women and Brahmins
english_translation:
The cow, the woman, the sacred Brahmins true,
And men in holy garb whom the Devas acclaim,
These the king shall protect; if that duty he ignores,
Irredeemable his hell shall be, cursed ever his name.
notes: It is the duty of the ruler to protect the cow, the woman, the brahmins true and the devout true. If he fails, he shall surely be condemned to hell.

english_title: Ruler's Share—One-Sixth of the Subject's Produce
english_translation:
If salvation high and treasures true you seek,
Then, awake or asleep, unceasing, the holy way pursue;
Know that of labour done in this sea-girt world,
To the King, in truth, one share in six is due.
notes: The ruler has a claim to one-sixth of the produce of his subjects. Let him not go beyond this. That is not the dharmic way.

english_title: Ruler's Duty to Defend the Territory
english_translation:
If the ruler exceeding well his state protects,
The subjects, in duty bound, to that same end incline;
When the enemy, in lust of pride, the state invades,
Then, like a leopard, leaps the king to defend his domain.
notes: It is the duty of the ruler to defend his people. Like a tiger he should spring on the invader. The ruler who protects his people wins the loyalty of his subjects.

english_translation:
Breath in control held, letting inward fire upward rise,
Mind turned to Samadhi moon-sprung nectar—if they drink not,
But, like inebriates, heady liquors madly consume,
Then, such shall by ruler to just punishment be brought.
notes: It is the duty of the ruler to punish those who indulge in inebriate drinking. True drinking is to reach the moon in samadhi and quaff of the divine nectar that flows from there.

english_title: Ruler to Punish Those Who Deviate From Their Professed Faiths
english_translation:
Who, by their professed faiths, do not abide,
Beside the judgement they receive in the life beyond,
In terms of Agamic law by Siva revealed,
Punished they shall be on earth by the just ruler of the land.
notes: Let each one stand constant in his own ordained faith. If they deviate, the ruler should not fail to punish them according to the laws laid down in the Agamas.

english_translation:
The fertilising flood of rains outpouring
Makes trees and plants bloom enriched with sap;
The areca palm, coconut, cane and plantain green.
And nux vomica — stand laden rich with crop.
notes: The rains fertilise the earth. All nature wears a green mantle. The trees grow and plants bloom enriched with sap. The palms, the coconut and areca, rise tall and high. The cane gets its sugary sucrose; the plantain yields its delicious fruits. Even the bitter nux vomica so dear to yogic practices flourish because of rain.

english_translation:
The mountain torrent rushes down from the heights,
Boundless like the love from the pure heart,
Foamless, stainless, clear and crystalline,
It is fit for bathing the Lord.
